author: IGN
description:
Ghost of Yotei's Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted DLC, reviewed by Michael Higham on PlayStation 5.

"This wave of paid DLC for Ghost of Yotei is a great reminder of just how graceful and deadly its combat can be, especially with how it's further emphasized in the new run-based Most Wanted mode. I didn't expect to get the itch for another run each time I was struck down, but that speaks to Yotei’s satisfying swordplay and the way these remixed challenges pushed me to think harder about every tool available. Echoes of Sekigahara isn't groundbreaking as an extension of the existing story, but Atsu gets a brief moment to shine again and show a more vulnerable, intimate side alongside a charming foil from her past. The battles within are familiar and the views are still impressive, but this one-two punch is a reminder of how fundamentally great Sucker Punch's ronin fantasy has been, and a layup for anyone looking for an excuse to return to Ghost of Yotei."

#IGN
title: Ghost of Yotei DLC Review – Echoes Of Sekigahara and Most Wanted

Take a look at the Official Trailer for Capturing Bigfoot, a documentary following the story of Roger Patterson’s pursuit of Bigfoot, distributed by XYZ Films. Navigate the woods of Northern California in Capturing Bigfoot, coming soon.

The documentary follows the story of Roger Patterson’s pursuit of Bigfoot, who on October 20, 1967, captured 59 seconds of film showing a creature (dubbed “Patty”) walking through the woods of Northern California—footage that became the most analyzed and debated in history. When a reel of 16mm film discovered in a safe five decades later blows the legend wide open, the people who were there come together to give the full picture. 

Director Marq Evans (“Claydream”) and producer Tamir Ardon (“Claydream,” “Skywalkers: A Love Story”) infuse this story of family and fabulists with a striking emotional heft, featuring never-before-seen archival footage and original interviews with figures both famous and infamous within the vibrant Bigfoot community. author: IGN
description:
Gears of War: E-Day reviewed by Ryan McCaffrey on Xbox Series X, also available on PC.

"By going back to the beginning, Gears of War: E-Day returns to the heart of this series: Marcus Fenix, Dom Santiago, and a Locust horde that’s as terrifying as it is dangerous. E-Day pulls off the tightrope act of giving us a heartfelt prequel with strong characters even when we know how it ends. On a more mechanical level, it also evolves the enemies, weapons, and combat you’d expect to deliver a Gears of War campaign that stands toe-to-toe with any of the others. It wraps up with 10 years still left to go before Marcus gets tossed in prison ahead of the events of the first Gears of War, so here’s hoping the next one stays in the past for a while longer – and that we don’t have to wait another seven years for it to arrive."
title: Gears of War: E-Day Campaign Review
